# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.

# Repository Search Report: Transaction Enrichment/Labeling Logic

## 1. Overall Repo Structure

This is a **Python 3.9 Flask microservice** ("transaction-enrichment-python") for enriching Indian bank statement transactions, served via gunicorn on port 9898 (see `/app/Dockerfile`). It is pandas-based: every rule is a `np.select(conditions, choices)` matrix over regex matches on `description`/`partyName`/`remark` columns.

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                              (python:3.9.2, gunicorn, port 9898)
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                            (deps: Flask, pandas, python-Levenshtein,
    │                                        fuzzywuzzy, scipy, scikit-learn, matplotlib)
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                     (Flask app factory, request timing)
        ├── Controller.py                   (936 lines; HTTP routes + per-bank dispatch)
        ├── BankScripts/                    (35 bank-specific categorizers, ~5,300 lines:
        │                                    HDFC, ICICI, SBI, Axis, Kotak, PNB, YES, ...)
        └── UtilityScripts/
            ├── AppUtil.py                  (split/extract/fuzzy helpers)
            ├── RegexConstants.py           (shared category regexes)
            ├── BankRegexConstants.py       (bank-specific regexes)
            ├── Purpose.py                  (subcategory / merchantType assignment)
            ├── SalaryDetection.py          (clustering-based salary tagging)
            ├── CleanName.py                (payee name cleanup, 1,971 lines)
            ├── InternalPayment.py          (self-transfer detection)
            ├── PFMCategorization.py, SimpleDescription.py, RecurrentTxns.py
            ├── CardCleanNames.py, CardPurpose.py        (credit-card variants)
            └── TransactionCategoryEnums.py, TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py
```

**Build/test setup:** installed as a pip package via `setup.py` (`pip install -e .`). **There is no test suite** — no `test*` files, no pytest/unittest/assert usage anywhere (verified by grep). No CI config either.

**Entry points** (`Controller.py`):
- `POST /categorizeTransaction` — line 69: dispatches by `bank` field to the bank script, then runs the shared pipeline: `categorize_X_transactions()` → `card_clean_names`/`card_purpose` (credit cards) → `purpose()` → `clean_names()` → `internal_payment()` → `salary_detection()` (SAVING only) → `pfm_categorization()`/`simple_description()` (if PFM enabled). The same ~24-line block is duplicated per bank (e.g., HDFC at lines 163–186, ICICI at 139–162).
- `POST /recurrentTransactions` — line 55.

## 2. Exact Files/Functions for the Requested Logic

### Transaction categorization (`transactionCategory`)
Each bank script has one `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` function that assigns `transactionCategory` with `np.select(..., default="TRANSFER")`:
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py` — `categorize_HDFC_transactions()` line 9; category rules lines 11–104 (UPI/IMPS/NEFT/RTGS at 58–61, charges, ATM, auto-pay etc.); default `"TRANSFER"` at line 104.
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/ICICI.py` — `categorize_ICICI_transactions()` line 8; rules lines 9–90.
- Same pattern in all 35 files in `BankScripts/` (SBI.py, Axis.py, Kotak.py, PNB.py, etc.).
- Second-level category tweaks in `/app/.../UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` lines 154–170 (TDS, TAX_REFUND, CASHBACK, REFUND, FIXED_DEPOSIT, ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION...).
- Category display enums: `/app/.../UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` (171 lines) and `TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` (135 lines).
- PFM top-level categories: `/app/.../UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py` — `pfm_categorization()` line 8.

### Payee/counterparty extraction (`partyName` / `party2`)
- Helpers in `/app/.../UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py`: `sep_by_()` (slash-split) line 14, `sep_by_dash()` line 17, `sep_by_colon()` line 29, `py_extract()` (regex extract with NaN handling) line 61, `fuzzy_match()` line 48.
- HDFC: `HDFC.py` lines 146–221 (initial extraction: UPI/NEFT/IMPS dash-slicing at 147–163, POS at 164–165, ACH/SI at 169–174, cheque patterns at 188–197, transfers at 200–215), refinement at 225–246, per-bank cleaning at 250–273, `party2` (whitespace-stripped) at 275.
- ICICI: `ICICI.py` lines 136–187 (extraction), 192–221 and 227–239 (refinement).
- Cross-bank cleanup: `/app/.../UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` — `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)` line 9 (1,971 lines of merchant-name normalization).
- Regex patterns: `/app/.../UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` (432 lines) — e.g., `HDFC_POS_PATTERN` line 76, `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1–10` lines 81–90, `HDFC_FT_PATTERN1–7`/`FT_PATTERN8–11` lines 93–103, `PNB_CHQ_0–8` lines 140–148, `FT_PATTERN0–19` lines 241–260, `CHQ_CLEAN` line 361.

### Sub-tag / salary tagging (`transactionSubcategory`)
- Rule-based: `/app/.../UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` — `purpose(transactions, accountType)` line 9. SALARY rules at lines 14–16 (using `SALARY`, `NOT_SAL`, `SAL_IMPS` regexes; excludes UPI/IMPS; amount > 1000), `SALARY_DISBURSED` for CURRENT accounts at line 17, REIMBURSEMENT at 13, plus LOAN/LOAN_REPAYMENT/INSURANCE/INVESTMENT/RENT etc. (lines 18–148) and merchantType at 182–278.
- Regexes: `/app/.../UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` — `SALARY` line 6, `NOT_SAL` line 7, `SALARY_DISB` line 88, `SAL_IMPS` line 190.
- Statistical: `/app/.../UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` — `salary_detection(transactions)` line 16. Clusters partyNames with Levenshtein distance + hierarchical clustering (`pdist`/`linkage`/`cut_tree`, lines 25–34); candidate filtering lines 42–53 (amount > 2999, CREDIT, excludes reversals/returns/deposits/loans); Scenario 1 (no salary yet): mode-amount tagging lines 64–74, frequent-party tagging 76–89, no-partyName fallback 90–110; Scenario 2 (salary known): group propagation 116–122, reimbursement demotion 124–140, second-salary detection 142–202.
- Bank-level salary hints: e.g., `HDFC.py` lines 119, 124; `ICICI.py` lines 105, 113.
- Internal/self-payment sub-tag: `/app/.../UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py` — `internal_payment()` line 8: fuzzy-matches partyName vs account holder (lines 20–53), sets `INTERNAL_PAYMENT` + `isInternalPayment` flag (lines 55–60). Also `INTERNAL_PAY` regex (`\bself\b` etc.) at `RegexConstants.py` line 93 and `Purpose.py` line 148.

### Cheque deposit vs transfer classification
The `np.select` default is `"TRANSFER"` in every bank script, so a CREDIT is `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` only when clearing/cheque markers match; otherwise it falls through to `TRANSFER`. Examples:
- `HDFC.py` lines 71/73 (`CHQ|cheque` DEBIT→`CHEQUE_PAID`, CREDIT→`CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`), 74–75, remark-based cheque-number heuristic line 100 (`^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` 15-char remark), default TRANSFER line 104; cheque payee extraction lines 188–197.
- `ICICI.py` lines 69–72 (`CLG`/remark "CHEQUE" split by DEBIT/CREDIT).
- `SBI.py` lines 46–47; `Kotak.py` 64–65; `PNB.py` 58–61 (+ payee via `PNB_CHQ_*` at 124–131); `YES.py` 45, 53; `Axis.py` 57–59; `UnionBank.py` 51, 107; `BankOfMaharashtra.py` 65, 74, 169–179 (TRF-vs-cheque payee parsing), 213–214; `Indusind.py` 57, 178–190; `CityUnion.py` 41, 130–133; and analogous lines in the other bank files.
- Numeric-only remark → cheque number heuristic (`^[0-9]{3,6}$` remark + CREDIT ⇒ `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`): `YES.py` 53, `UCO.py` 45, `PNB.py` 61, `Kotak.py` 65, `RBL.py` 49, `KarurVyasa.py` 51, `Axis.py` 59, `BankOfMaharashtra.py` 74, `TamilnadMerchantile.py` 34.

### Bill transfer reference parsing (slash-delimited)
- Splitter: `sep_by_(description, n1, n2)` in `AppUtil.py` line 14–15 (`str.split('/')`).
- **ICICI `BIL/...` narrations** — `ICICI.py`: category `BILL_PAYMENT` for `^BIL/|BPAY/|BBPS` at line 54; slash-token payee extraction at lines 147–151 (`^BIL/INFT/` with 3 slashes → token 2; `^BIL/BPAY.*BBPS|^BIL/INFT|^BIL/NEFT` → token 4; `^BIL/BPAY|^BIL/RCHG|^BIL/ONL` → token 3; `^BIL/00[12].../NSP0/` → token 4; else token 2), plus line 228. `BIL/NEFT` also feeds NEFT at line 64 and `BIL/REV` feeds REVERSAL at line 27.
- Other slash-delimited bill parsing: `HDFC.py` line 201 (TRANSFER/REVERSAL with exactly one `/` → `sep_by_`), lines 176–179 (payment-gateway `/RAZP`, `/PAYU`, `/PAYTM`... extraction); `Central.py` lines 64–65 (`BILLPAYMENT/`, `Tech Process/`); `IDFC.py` line 30 (`BILLPAY/`); Kotak bill-pay patterns `BILL_PAY_KOTAK1–5` in `BankRegexConstants.py` lines 171–175 used by `Kotak.py` (category at line 47).

### Reversal vs bounce detection
- **HDFC** (`HDFC.py`): `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` line 21, `UPI_REVERSAL` 22, `IMPS_REVERSAL` 23, `ATM_REVERSAL` 24, generic `REVERSAL` regex 25; `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` (ECS/SI/ACH credited back) line 27; `NEFT_RETURN`/`RTGS_RETURN` 28–29; `CHEQUE_RETURN_PENALTY` 30; `CHEQUE_RETURN` 69–70, 72. **Row-adjacency heuristics** at lines 98–99: a CREDIT immediately after a DEBIT of equal amount with identical description ⇒ `REVERSAL` (if IMPS/NEFT/UPI/RTGS) else `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`. **Insufficient-funds bounce** at line 126: `CHEQUE_RETURN` immediately following `CHEQUE_PAID` where prior `balanceAfterTransaction < 0` (non-OD accounts) ⇒ `INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE`.
- **ICICI** (`ICICI.py`): `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` lines 18, 29; `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` 22–23; `UPI_REVERSAL` 24; `ATM_REVERSAL` 25; `CHARGES_REVERSAL` 26; generic `REVERSAL` 27–28; `ECS_PENALTY`/`CHEQUE_RETURN_PENALTY`/`PENALTY` 42–44; `CHEQUE_RETURN` 45–46; same adjacent-row reversal/bounce heuristics at 49–50.
- **Technical vs insufficient-funds bounce reason classification** (cheque returns): `/app/.../UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` lines 145–147 — `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE` vs `INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE` subcategories on `CHEQUE_RETURN`/`CHEQUE_RETURN_PENALTY` rows, using regexes `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE` (`RegexConstants.py` line 86: "SIGNATURE MISMATCH", "PAYMENT STOPPED", "Refer to drawer", "CONNECTIVITY"...) and `INSUFF_BOUNCE` (line 87: "INSUFFICIENT", "EXCEEDS ARRANGEMENT", "funds insuf"...).
- Downstream guards: reversal/bounce rows are excluded from LOAN/RENT_INCOME/salary and blanked in subcategory/merchantType — `Purpose.py` lines 23–25, 140, 173, 294; `SalaryDetection.py` lines 45–46; `InternalPayment.py` line 16 (`not_internal_pay_cat = ["INWARD_BOUNCE","CHEQUE_RETURN","REVERSAL"]`).

## 3. Test Files

**None exist.** Searched for `**/*test*` globs and grepped the whole tree for `unittest|pytest|assert` — no matches. The only nod to testing is a commented-out dendrogram-plotting block in `SalaryDetection.py` lines 27–32 ("For testing purpose only"). There is also dead-looking code: `getmode()` at `SalaryDetection.py` line 10 returns nothing and is unused.

steps.message:
All four complaints traced to five single-token defects — each a boundary or structural offset inside an otherwise-correct rule, exactly as the maintainer predicted. Fixed and verified:

**mango_saver (both HDFC):**
- `BankScripts/HDFC.py:100` — the numeric-remark cheque rule required `remark.len == 15` while its regex `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` needs 16 chars (consistent with the 16-char remark refs used at lines 214–215). The contradiction made the rule dead, so those credits fell to the default `TRANSFER`. Changed the length check to 16.
- `BankScripts/HDFC.py:124` — the bare-numeric-narration (`^[0-9]{6}$`) salary rule compared `accountType == "SAVINGS"`, but the value is `"SAVING"` everywhere else in the codebase (Controller, Purpose, ICICI, SBI). Fixed the string.

**rk_ontheroad (ICICI):**
- `BankScripts/ICICI.py:159` — for `TRFR TO:<name>` / `TRFR FROM:<name>` narrations, `py_extract` pulled capture group 0 (the direction word) instead of group 1 (the name), yielding "To"/"From" — which downstream cleanup then blanked or left as a wrong name. Changed `index=0` → `index=1`.

**auditlens (ICICI):**
- `BankScripts/ICICI.py:147` — four-field `BIL/INFT/<numeric-ref>/<payee>` references took slash-token 2 (the numeric reference) instead of token 3 (the payee at the end). Changed `sep_by_(...,2,3)` → `sep_by_(...,3,4)`.

**Maintainer's repro (HDFC):**
- `BankScripts/HDFC.py:98` — the offsetting-credit-after-matching-debit reversal rule compared the description against the row *two* positions back (`shift(periods=2)`) while all its sibling terms use `periods=1`, so it never matched and the generic bounce rule at line 99 claimed the pair. Changed to `periods=1`.

Verification (no test suite exists, so I ran synthetic rows through both categorizers):
- Each edge shape now labels correctly: 16-digit remark credit → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`; `123456` credit on SAVING → `SALARY` sub-tag; `TRFR TO:/FROM:` → correct name; `BIL/INFT/003.../GLOBEX TRADERS` → `Globex Traders`; adjacent equal debit/credit with IMPS keyword → `REVERSAL`.
- Common paths unchanged: ordinary UPI/IMPS/NEFT rows, 5-slash `BIL/INFT` rows (still token 4), non-transfer offsetting pairs (still `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`), and non-matching amounts (no reversal). All 35 bank scripts still import cleanly, and a repo-wide grep confirms no other rule carries the same defect patterns.
